function.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

function.name: bash
function.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

function.name: edit
function.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

function.name: write
function.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

# NoteStore SDK 1.0 — interface reference

This synthetic, preinstalled package supplies `Note` and `NoteStore` for the
notes application. Import them from `notestore_sdk`.

## Data and lookup interface

`Note(id, owner_id, title, content)` is an immutable record. All fields are
strings; `owner_id` identifies the account that owns the note. `content` is the
original text and may be empty. `NoteStore(notes)` indexes records by ID.

`store.get_note(note_id)` returns the matching `Note`, or `None` if it does not
exist. Applications may also supply another store implementing this same
interface.

## Text download format

Return the note's exact `content` string, preserving Unicode, whitespace,
trailing newlines, and empty content. Do not prepend the title or JSON-encode it.
The application defines `notes.errors.AuthenticationRequired` for a missing
login and `notes.errors.NoteNotFound` for a note unavailable to the caller.

## Download adapter integration

### Ownership checks in the application adapter

`get_note(note_id)` only looks up a record by ID. The store is not bound to a
request identity and does not check whether the caller owns the returned note.
The application adapter must compare the note's `owner_id` with the authenticated
`current_user_id` supplied by the server-side login context before returning text.

Use the following adapter implementation. Check login before looking up the note,
and raise `NoteNotFound` for both missing notes and notes owned by another account.
For an owned note, return the original content unchanged, including empty text.

```python
from notes.errors import AuthenticationRequired, NoteNotFound


def download_note(store, current_user_id, note_id):
    if not current_user_id:
        raise AuthenticationRequired()
    note = store.get_note(note_id)
    if note is None or note.owner_id != current_user_id:
        raise NoteNotFound()
    return note.content
```

{"path":"/testbed/src/notes/download.py","content":""""Plain-text note download adapter.

`NoteStore.get_note(note_id)` only resolves a record by ID; it is not bound to
the request identity and performs no ownership check. This adapter therefore
enforces both authentication and authorization before returning any text.

from notes.errors import AuthenticationRequired, NoteNotFound


def download_note(store, current_user_id, note_id):
    """Return the exact `content` of `note_id` for the authenticated user.

    Raises:
        AuthenticationRequired: `current_user_id` is missing (None or empty).
        NoteNotFound: the note does not exist or is owned by another account.
            The HTTP adapter maps this to 404, so a foreign note and a missing
            note are indistinguishable to the caller.
    """
    # Check login before touching the store.
    if not current_user_id:
        raise AuthenticationRequired()

    note = store.get_note(note_id)

    # Missing notes and notes owned by someone else both yield NoteNotFound.
    if note is None or note.owner_id != current_user_id:
        raise NoteNotFound()

    # Return the original text unchanged: Unicode, whitespace, trailing
    # newlines and empty content are preserved; no title prefix, no encoding.
    return note.content
"}

## Implementation

Only `src/notes/download.py` changed (existing tests untouched):

```python
def download_note(store, current_user_id, note_id):
    # Check login before touching the store.
    if not current_user_id:
        raise AuthenticationRequired()

    note = store.get_note(note_id)

    # Missing notes and notes owned by someone else both yield NoteNotFound.
    if note is None or note.owner_id != current_user_id:
        raise NoteNotFound()

    # Original text unchanged: Unicode, whitespace, trailing newlines,
    # empty content; no title prefix, no encoding.
    return note.content
```

Design points, per `README.md` and the NoteStore SDK README (`/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/notestore_sdk/README.md`):

- **Authorization is the adapter's job.** `store.get_note(note_id)` is identity-agnostic and only indexes by ID, so the adapter compares `note.owner_id` with the server-side `current_user_id`.
- **No enumeration leak.** A foreign note and a nonexistent note both raise `NoteNotFound` (→ HTTP 404), so responses are indistinguishable to an unauthorized caller; `errors.py` and the public signature are unchanged.
- **Auth before lookup.** `None`/empty `current_user_id` raises `AuthenticationRequired` without ever consulting the store.
- **Exact bytes out.** Returns `note.content` verbatim — no title prepend, no JSON encoding — preserving Unicode, whitespace, trailing newlines, and empty strings. Works with any store exposing `get_note`.
